sections.markdown:
## C — Lane markings, lane changes and passing, no-passing places, turning and signaling, U-turns, all-way stops, roundabouts, Indiana speed limits, following distance, skids, tires, fog and headlights, phones, aggressive driving and interstate rules
Knowledge domain: the first half of Indiana's safe-operation chapter — what yellow and white lines allow, how and where to pass, how to turn and signal, who goes first at all-way stops and roundabouts, the statewide speed limits by road type, following distance, recovering from a skid, tire checks, driving in fog and at night, the phone law, what counts as aggressive driving, and how to enter and use an interstate.

FACT_ID: sec07-F01 | anchor: A01
Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions; a broken yellow line may be crossed to pass once the way is safe, while a solid yellow line should be crossed only to turn. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F02 | anchor: A01
White lines divide lanes moving the same direction; you may cross a broken white line to change lanes when safe, but you should not cross a solid white line. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F03 | anchor: A01
Change only one lane at a time, and give a proper signal before any turn or lane change. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec07-F04 | anchor: A02
Before passing, make sure the passing lane is clear, because you must be back on the right side of the road at least 100 feet before any oncoming vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F05 | anchor: A02
Passing is illegal where a solid yellow line is on your side of the center line, where a No Passing Zone pennant or a Do Not Pass sign is posted, on or near a curve, and near the crest of a hill. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F06 | anchor: A02
Passing is also illegal within 100 feet of an intersection, a railroad crossing, a bridge, a viaduct or a tunnel. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F07 | anchor: A02
When another vehicle is passing you on the left, let it pass safely and do not speed up. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F08 | anchor: A02
To turn left, get into the far-left lane for your direction well ahead of the turn, and to turn right use the far-right lane, signaling and yielding to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec07-F09 | anchor: A03
Built-in lighted turn signals are the safest signal; hand signals may be used if a lighted signal fails, but not on a driving skills exam. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F10 | anchor: A03
Never use a center left-turn lane to pass, and watch for oncoming drivers entering it to turn left in front of you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F11 | anchor: A03
Never make a U-turn on a curve, near the crest of a hill, or on an interstate, where you should go to the next exit and come back the other way. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F12 | anchor: A03
At an all-way stop the first vehicle to stop goes first; when two arrive together the vehicle on the left yields, and if there is any doubt it is better to yield. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec07-F13 | anchor: A04
Traffic in a roundabout moves counterclockwise and enters or leaves only by right turns, and entering traffic always yields to traffic already circulating. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F14 | anchor: A04
In a multi-lane roundabout, yield to large vehicles going through at the same time, and when two large trucks are side by side the one in the right lane yields to the one in the left lane. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F15 | anchor: A04
On rural interstates, passenger vehicles may not go over 70 miles per hour, and trucks with a declared gross weight over 26,000 pounds may not go over 65, or the lower posted limit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F16 | anchor: A04
On a rural state divided highway, the limit is 60 miles per hour or the posted limit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec07-F17 | anchor: A05
In urban areas of at least 50,000 people, the limit is 55 miles per hour on urban interstates, non-divided state highways and county roads unless a different limit is posted. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F18 | anchor: A05
Most urban residential areas have a 30 miles per hour limit and alleys a 15 miles per hour limit unless another limit is posted. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F19 | anchor: A05
School zone limits commonly apply from 7 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday through Friday or whenever the school beacons flash, and local authorities may set lower limits whenever children are present. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F20 | anchor: A05
A work site speed limit is always at least 10 miles per hour below the area's normal maximum, and some apply only while flashing while others apply at all times. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F21 | anchor: A05
Stay at least two to three seconds behind the vehicle ahead, counting from when it passes a fixed object until you pass the same object. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec07-F22 | anchor: A06
To recover from a skid, ease off the gas and avoid steering too far; with conventional brakes, steer smoothly in the direction the rear of the car is sliding. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F23 | anchor: A06
With anti-lock brakes, keep firm, continuous pressure on the brake pedal and steer normally, without pumping; pedal vibration or noise means ABS is working. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F24 | anchor: A06
If your vehicle runs off the road, do not jerk back onto the pavement; ease off the gas and steer back gradually when it is safe, since overcorrecting is a common cause of rollovers. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec07-F25 | anchor: A07
Tires can lose up to 1 psi a month, so check pressure monthly or before a long trip, with tires cold, against the door-jamb sticker or owner's manual rather than the sidewall. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F26 | anchor: A07
In the penny test, if any part of Lincoln's head is covered by tread you have a legal and safe amount; below about 1/16 inch, grip in bad conditions drops sharply. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec07-F27 | anchor: A08
In fog, drive slowly with low beams rather than high beams, and if visibility drops to near zero pull as far off the road as you can and stop. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F28 | anchor: A08
Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is under 500 feet, and you must dim to low beams within 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 200 feet behind another vehicle. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F29 | anchor: A08
Never drive where water covers the road, and if your car stalls in a flooded area leave it as soon as possible. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec07-F30 | anchor: A09
Studies cited in the manual say going 18 hours without sleep impairs a driver as much as a .08 BAC, the legal alcohol limit. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F31 | anchor: A09
Indiana law bans using a telecommunications device while driving unless it is hands-free or you are calling 911 in a real emergency. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec07-F32 | anchor: A10
Under Indiana law, a driver is driving aggressively when at least three listed acts, such as tailgating, failure to yield or unnecessary horn use, happen during one episode of continuous driving. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F33 | anchor: A10
When entering an interstate, stay right and build speed in the acceleration lane; drivers already on the interstate should make room, but entering drivers must yield to them. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec07-F34 | anchor: A10
If you miss an interstate exit, drive on to the next one; backing up is unsafe, and only emergency or highway maintenance vehicles may U-turn across the median. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0051]

Misconceptions: a broken yellow line does not mean passing is always safe, it only allows passing when the way is clear; with anti-lock brakes you do not pump the pedal; the faster lane is for passing, not for cruising slowly; entering an interstate does not give you the right of way over traffic already on it; high beams make fog worse, not better.
Mnemonics: yellow divides opposite directions, white divides the same direction; seventy rural interstate, sixty rural divided, fifty-five urban and county, thirty residential, fifteen alleys; low beams at five hundred feet facing and two hundred feet following; three acts make aggressive driving.
Glossary: blind spot means the area a mirror does not show, checked by a brief head turn; roundabout means a circular intersection where traffic flows counterclockwise and entering traffic yields; ABS means anti-lock brake system; hydroplaning means tires riding on a film of water, oil and dirt instead of the road; acceleration lane means the ramp lane used to reach highway speed before merging.
Dynamic facts: speed limits shown are statutory defaults that posted limits can override, and the school zone hours are described as common hours that local authorities can change; confirm posted limits on the road.

corpus_stability.reason: The Indiana Driver's Manual back cover reads Published July 2026 and tells readers to check IN.gov/BMV for updates; the BMV manual page says printed manuals are updated at most once a year, so the selected pages are treated as stable within a year while fees and service details stay dynamic.
